summary: 79-year-old thin woman with a small, firm, non-tender right groin lump below and lateral to the pubic tubercle for 6 weeks, not reducible, no obstructive symptoms. Femoral hernias carry the highest strangulation risk: early (urgent elective) repair, not watchful waiting or a truss.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Small lump at the top of the right thigh
inputs.hpi: Noticed a small lump at the top of her right thigh six weeks ago. Occasionally aches when walking to the shops. Has not been able to push it back. Eating and drinking normally, bowels regular. No vomiting.

exam.abdomen: Soft, non-tender, not distended. 2 cm firm, non-tender swelling below the inguinal ligament, lateral and inferior to the right pubic tubercle, irreducible, no cough impulse, no skin change. Not pulsatile. No lymphadenopathy elsewhere.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Right femoral hernia (irreducible, non-tender)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Right femoral hernia in a 79-year-old woman — irreducible but non-tender, no obstruction. High strangulation risk: book urgent repair (laparoscopic or open preperitoneal/low approach).

mustRankTopK.note: Lump below and lateral to the pubic tubercle in an elderly woman.
mustRankTopK.knownGapNote: PANE top 3 = cholecystitis, GORD, diverticulitis; femoral_hernia is not listed despite groin_swelling. PANE: unlisted features count at DEFAULT_SENSITIVITY 0.30 for every disease and there is no false-positive term, so high-prior abdominal diseases (cholecystitis 0.15, GORD 0.12, PUD 0.10; male inguinal hernia x5) outrank the organ-specific disease after a single non-abdominal feature.
mustRankTopK.proposedFix: Model P(feature | not disease) or use a low default sensitivity (e.g. <=0.05) for features outside a disease's system; restrict the candidate set by the presenting system (breast / neck / groin).

emergencyLevel.note: Not an emergency today, but must not sit on a routine list.
emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Web, since the engine-matching fixes (2026-09): this passed only because triage read negated phrases in the free text as positive findings (lost reasons: Vomiting or possible dehydration). With negation-aware matching web triage gives acuity=routine, action=routine_booking, score=12: no triage rule covers this presentation.

mustInclude.note: HerniaSurge: femoral hernias should be repaired urgently/early; laparoscopic repair suggested where expertise exists.

mustExclude.note: Watchful waiting or a truss is inappropriate for a femoral hernia.

dxVariant.note: Irreducible but non-tender: the incarcerated variant (urgent, not emergency) fits best.

guideline.name: HerniaSurge — International guidelines for groin hernia management
guideline.section: Diagnosis (clinical examination, ultrasound for uncertain swellings); watchful waiting in minimally symptomatic men; mesh repair (Lichtenstein, TEP/TAPP); groin hernia in women; femoral hernia; emergency repair
guideline.citation: HerniaSurge Group. International guidelines for groin hernia management. Hernia. 2018;22:1–165.

guideline.name: WSES guidelines — emergency repair of complicated abdominal wall hernias (2017 update)
guideline.section: Diagnosis of strangulation (clinical signs, lactate, CPK, D-dimer, CT); timing of surgery; manual reduction only without strangulation; mesh in clean (CDC I) and clean-contaminated fields
guideline.citation: Birindelli A, Sartelli M, Di Saverio S, et al. 2017 update of the WSES guidelines for emergency repair of complicated abdominal wall hernias. World J Emerg Surg. 2017;12:37.

rationale: Base femoral case. Elderly thin woman; lump below the inguinal ligament; irreducible but not tender. Tests femoral recognition and early repair. The CC is presentation-based ("lump at the top of the thigh").
